question_text: Assuming that all of the valence electrons contribute to current flow, (a) calculate the mobility of an electron in copper and (b) calculate the average drift velocity for electrons in a 100 cm copper wire when 10 V are applied. The lattice parameter of copper is $3.6151 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~cm}$ and, since copper is FCC, there are four atoms/unit cell. The conductivity $\sigma=5.98 \times 10^{5} \Omega^{-1} \cdot \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}$. Give your answer as a tuple (mobility of an electron in copper, average drift velocity for electrons in a 100 cm copper wire when 10 V are applied).The units of each required answer are (cm^2/(V·s), cm/s), respectively.
response:
## Solution

**(a) Electron concentration**

Copper is FCC with 4 atoms/unit cell and contributes 1 valence electron per atom:

$$n = \frac{4 \text{ atoms/cell} \times 1 \text{ e}^{-}/\text{atom}}{a^3} = \frac{4}{(3.6151\times10^{-8}\,\text{cm})^3} = 8.466\times10^{22}\,\text{e}^{-}/\text{cm}^3$$

**(a) Mobility**

Using $\sigma = nq\mu$:

$$\mu = \frac{\sigma}{nq} = \frac{5.98\times10^{5}}{(8.466\times10^{22})(1.6\times10^{-19})} \approx 44.15\,\text{cm}^2/(\text{V·s})$$

**(b) Drift velocity**

The electric field in the wire is $E = V/L = 10/100 = 0.1\,\text{V/cm}$, so

$$v_d = \mu E = (44.15)(0.1) \approx 4.41\,\text{cm/s}$$

$$\boxed{(44.15,\ 4.41)}$$
